title: Patience through Him
hookLine: be patient, and your patience is only through Allah (16:127)
tomorrow: By night, from mosque to mosque
last: HIKMAH — ARGUE IN THE BEST WAY.

cards: You've told yourself to be patient a hundred times. Count to ten. Breathe.
Don't send it. Sometimes it works, and sometimes, on the eleventh count, you send it anyway. Patience is hard to manufacture on command.
The last verses of An-Nahl know this. They're said, in the commentaries, to come at one of the most painful moments of the Prophet's life, and their answer is not try harder. It's something stranger.

teach.b: Many commentators connect these verses to the battle of Uhud. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ found the body of his uncle Hamza, killed and mutilated, and in his grief, the reports say, he spoke of repaying it many times over.

teach.h: ONLY TO THE MEASURE OF THE HARM.
teach.b: Verse 126 answers: if you punish, punish only to the measure of the harm done to you. But if you're patient, that is better for the patient. Then verse 127 speaks to him directly.
In Pickthall's words: "Thine endurance is only by (the help of) Allah." The verse gives a command, be patient, and in the same breath says you can't do it alone.

Sabr comes from a root meaning to hold back, to restrain, to keep something in place. Arabic speakers use it for holding yourself steady when everything in you wants to lurch. And the verse says that steadiness is given.
It goes on: don't grieve over them, and don't be distressed by their schemes. Then the surah's last line: God is with those who are mindful of Him and those who do good.
Muhsinun, people of ihsan, the excellence of verse ninety.
A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari puts it from another side: whoever tries to be patient, God will make them patient, and no one is given a gift better or wider than patience.
So patience isn't a muscle you build alone, or only a mood that falls on you.
You reach for it, and it's handed to you.

teach.h: YOUR PATIENCE IS ONLY THROUGH GOD.
teach.b: The surah of gifts, uncountable favors, milk, honey, wisdom, closes by naming patience as one more of them.

how: Muslims speak of sabr as one of the central virtues and often ask God for patience in du'a; 16:126–128 is cited in teaching on restraint, proportion in retaliation and forgiveness.

o: patience: holding steady, a gift you reach for
hiding your grief so no one can see it
waiting quietly while doing nothing at all

games.q: the end of An-Nahl — tap the pairs.
p: punish only to the measure of harm
your patience is only through God
to hold back, to hold steady

s: 16:127 says patience comes from willpower alone
it commands patience and says it is only through God.
the commentators link these verses to Uhud
many connect them to the Prophet's grief over his uncle Hamza.
An-Nahl ends by mentioning the muhsinun
God is with the mindful and those who do good: the people of ihsan.

games.q: your uncle has been killed and mutilated, and you're grieving. the verses come. what do they allow you?
o: punish only to the measure of the harm; patience is better.
nothing at all; any response is forbidden.
games.why: 16:126 limits any response to the harm done, then says patience is better, and 16:127 says that patience comes through God.

practice: Think of the place in your life where patience is running out, a person, a wait, a body that isn't healing fast enough, and feel where it sits, maybe in your jaw or your chest. Breathe there.
If you pray, ask God for patience with that one thing in your own words; if not, notice you're asking for something you can't produce by force, and let the asking be enough.

wordCard.voice: Sabr. Patience, holding steady: commanded and given in the same verse, the last gift named in the surah of the bee. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: patience, endurance; from a root meaning to hold back, to keep steady.

carryVoice: Your line: patience is from him. Commanded and given in the same breath. That's day four hundred fifty-six.

sources.q: Thine endurance is only by (the help of) Allah.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1469 (whoever seeks patience is given it)
Tafsir on 16:126 (Uhud and Hamza), e.g. Ibn Kathir
